fact: Road deaths in India rose from 146,133 in 2015 to 183,382 in 2025, roughly 21 every hour.
Govt plans to raise the online safe-driving test pass mark from 60% to 75%.
Vietnam requires a 91% pass mark on its driving test, yet its road fatality rate is 13 per lakh population (India: 16.2).
Singapore has no similarly tough driving test but only 1.4 road fatalities per lakh population.
E-challans worth Rs 23,000 crore remain unpaid across states (told to the Supreme Court).
A Delhi-registered BMW had 42 challans for driving without PUCC, showing repeat offenders face no consequence.
The editorial argues India needs attitudinal change and strict enforcement; attitudes will not change while fines go unpaid.

fact: Section 185: first-offence drunken driving is a fine up to Rs 10,000 and/or up to 6 months imprisonment.

fact: Section 194D: riding without a helmet is a Rs 1,000 fine and 3-month licence disqualification.

fact: Section 199B allows fines to rise annually by up to 10%; Section 210A lets States notify a 1-10x multiplier on fines.

fact: Section 183(1): over-speeding is Rs 1,000-2,000 for light motor vehicles and Rs 2,000-4,000 for medium vehicles; licence can be impounded for repeat offences.
